newsitem.title: USA: Criminal checks required of U.S. home health aides.
newsitem.headline: Criminal checks required of U.S. home health aides.

text.p: Home health aides would have to undergo criminal background checks and meet other new health care quality standards to work for Medicare programmes under new rules proposed Wednesday.

In its first major revision of the rules since 1973, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services said home health care agencies taking part in the Medicare programme would have to meet the new standards to improve quality of care for the elderly and the disabled. Their staff would have to undergo background checks.
"Home health aides care for our most frail and vulnerable citizens," health secretary Donna Shalala said in proposing the new rules for the roughly 9,000 agencies that provide Medicare home services.

The revised programme attempts to make agencies take more responsibility for evaluating and coordinating care and monitoring quality. The conditions for participating in Medicare focus on patient rights, patient assessment, and quality improvement, HHS said. Agencies would have to use standardised methods of assessing patients.
Home care is the fastest growing expenditure within Medicare, the federal health programme that covers all Americans over age 65 and many disabled people.
More than 10 percent of Medicare patients needed at least some home services last year, costing $18 billion.
